positions.name: MeridianGateJustification
positions.frame: why is the signed-manifest gate required for Meridian deploys?
positions.why: Both expressions come from Quinton and read together as cause-and-effect: the present-tense requirement (src-1) and the past-incident rationale (src-2) form a single directional account — the gate exists because unsigned artifacts already reached staging. The affect/power reads mark src-2 as the evidentiary grounding for src-1's mandate rather than a separate claim, so the two cohere as one justificatory unit even though src-1 is a decision-grade declarative and src-2 is an assertive claim citing evidence.

positions.name: MeridianGateSpecificationSummary
positions.frame: what are the settled Gate/Scope/Owner parameters recorded for this deployment decision?
positions.why: src-3, src-4, and src-5 are Xena's own bolded-label triad (Gate/Scope/Owner) noted by the style pass as a matched parallel set and by the conviction pass as uniformly decision-grade ratification entries — each stating a settled facet (requirement, scope, accountability) of the same gate rather than arguing for it. Read together they form one compressed specification record of the decision, distinct from Quinton's original justificatory statements.
